title: SpacePlayerData lifecycle, active planet/star ownership, and SpaceContext transitions
status: static follow-up complete; no runtime execution

evidence_policy.basis: committed static exports/decomp-gap plus read-only Ghidra inspection of the existing SporeApp.exe snapshot
evidence_policy.important_rule: SDK names and offsets establish layout/type provenance; they do not by themselves prove function identity, ownership, runtime ordering, or enum aliasing.

read_only_inspection.project_source: existing SporeProject database copied to a temporary directory
read_only_inspection.note: The temporary inspection was used to recover current bodies, disassembly, direct references, and field mechanics; no new decompilation or project state was written to the repository.

executive_findings: 01021d40 allocates a 0x34-byte SpacePlayerData object, publishes it to Simulator::sSpacePlayerData at 0x016dda8c, explicitly initializes +0x04=0, +0x08=0, +0x0c=0, +0x10=-1, +0x18=-1, +0x1c=0, the three colony-vector words, and +0x14=1.0. It does not explicitly initialize +0x00 in the recovered body.

01021960 is a conditional SpaceContext writer: it stores the supplied integer at +0x10 only when the old value differs. The only special follow-up is new value 2 with non-null +0x08 and non-null return from 00ffbe50; it then calls 00c8b360 on the old +0x08 object and 01001360 with the helper result.

010219b0 is a reference-replacement routine for the SDK mpActiveStar (+0x08) and mpActivePlanet (+0x04) slots, not a context writer. It performs virtual intrusive-style AddRef/Release operations and clears the secondary/planet path when its second input is null or resolves to the same player object.
01001360 is a 917-byte collection/record refresh helper with its own reference-management operations. It is invoked by 01021960, 010213b0, and 010021a0; it does not itself write SpacePlayerData+0x10.

01022460 and 00bb7250 provide field-level teardown/release evidence. 01022460 clears and releases +0x04, +0x08, +0x0c, +0x1c, and the colony vector, and resets +0x18; 00bb7250 independently clears and releases +0x08.

The five +0x10 write sites recovered for this closure are 01021d40 initialization to -1, 01021960 conditional writes, and 01022580's independent conditional write to 0. The nine direct 01021960 callers request -1, 0, 1, or 2; requested value and actual store are distinct because 01021960 suppresses same-value writes.

00b60d80 is the only canonical caller of 01021d40, through a computed call at 00b622eb. The recovered 01021d40 body contains no whole-object free or old-global release; no direct final global nulling or whole-object teardown is established in this closure.

SpaceContext, cScenarioMode::mMode, and cGameInputManager::mCurrentGameMode remain separate state axes. The shared numeric value 2 is numerically coincidental, not an alias or proven transition mapping.

teardown.field_cleanup: 01022460 is the clearest committed static cleanup routine: it clears and releases +0x04, +0x08, +0x0c, +0x1c, releases the colony vector, and resets +0x18. 00bb7250 independently clears/releases +0x08.
teardown.context_cleanup: 01022460 does not write +0x10. The callers 00b32b20 and 00b32ce0 call 01022460 and then request 01021960(-1); 00b33350 calls 01022460 and conditionally requests 01021960(-1).
teardown.global_teardown: No direct final nulling or whole-object free of Simulator::sSpacePlayerData is present in the recovered global reference set. 01021d40 is allocation/publication, and 01022460 is field cleanup, not whole-object destruction.
teardown.runtime_limit: Static cleanup and release calls establish possible ownership operations, not runtime order or actual destruction.

unresolved_boundaries: The exact original ABI and semantic identities of 010219b0's two observed arguments remain unresolved; the prior three-parameter hypothesis is not promoted.
The exact roles of 00c8b360, 00ffbe50, and the 01001360 receiver/domain are not fully named by the committed static evidence.
No runtime order, same-value suppression frequency, or actual destruction order is claimed.
No whole-object destructor or final global release for Simulator::sSpacePlayerData is established.
The unowned 01022572 write reference is retained as unresolved and not used as lifecycle evidence.
SDK field names and intrusive_ptr types support owner roles but do not prove exact concrete dynamic types at every call site.
